Subject: Redline: order schedule caps/floors + packaging questions

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team reviewed the draft order schedule and attached a marked-up PDF (VeloxAI_Redlines_v3.pdf) with several pricing items that need clarification before we proceed to legal: 

- The "monthly cap" language in Exhibit A is ambiguous when autoscale credits are applied — is the cap applied pre- or post-credit?
- The floor/true-up definition doesn't specify invoicing cadence for burst credits and appears to let floors accumulate across SKUs; that could materially increase exposure for us.
- Packaging: how do you intend to map metered usage across bundled SKUs (we have three product SKUs that might be combined under a single commitment band).

We added suggested redline language and a short comment in the spreadsheet for an alternative true-up schedule.

Can we get Redwood's position on: (1) whether caps are net of credits, (2) a per-SKU floor aggregation rule (we'd prefer non-aggregation), and (3) an option to adopt a quarterly true-up instead of an annual true-up for the first 12 months?

We'd like a short call to resolve before legal exchange. Proposed availability: Mon 29th afternoon PT.

Regards,
Morgan Lee
Head of Procurement, VeloxAI

Attachments: VeloxAI_Redlines_v3.pdf (annotated), OrderSchedule_draft.xlsx (comment column)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Redline: order schedule caps/floors + packaging questions

Sean / team — I reviewed VeloxAI's annotated PDF and spreadsheet. High level legal positions and suggested contract text below. I've attached a one-page summary (Legal_annotated_points.pdf) for internal trace; will include suggested markups in the attached Drive link.

1) Caps and credits (position): Redwood's standard approach is to apply programmatic credits before evaluating the cap — i.e., billed tokens = raw usage - applied credits; cap triggers are evaluated on billed tokens. Suggested clause: 
"For clarity, any usage credits, promotional credits or autoscale credits shall be applied to raw usage prior to calculation of any monthly or annual cap. Caps shall therefore be evaluated against net billed usage."

Risk: this is clear operationally but could be interpreted to reduce customer's ability to carryforward credits. If Velox needs credits treated post-cap, we should ask for either a higher cap or a minimum committed spend (floor) reduction.

2) Floor aggregation (position): We propose a middle-ground: defaults to per-SKU floors, but with an optional aggregation election if the customer provides SKU mapping and consents to combined reporting. Suggested clause: 
"Order Schedule floors shall be calculated on a per-SKU basis unless Customer elects aggregation in writing and supplies a binding SKU mapping document no later than 30 days after Effective Date."

Operational note (Markus): per-SKU floors require an early mapping exercise; otherwise we can't guarantee invoice alignment.

3) True-up cadence (position): Quarterly true-up for year one is reasonable, subject to a cap on potential retroactive settlement liability. Suggested compromise clause: 
"For the Initial 12-month Term only, Customer may elect quarterly true-ups in lieu of annual true-ups, subject to a retroactive settlement cap equal to 25% of the aggregate committed spend for the quarter."

This 25% cap protects Redwood from outsized retroactive liabilities on large underreporting. If Velox pushes back, we can consider a higher cap in exchange for a higher minimum commit.

I'll prepare a tracked-change mark-up of Exhibit A and the order schedule by EOD Friday. Please confirm the proposed call time so we can share a short agenda (30–45 minutes): 
- confirm cap netting approach (10 min)
- floor aggregation and mapping (15 min)
- quarterly true-up guardrail and settlement cap (10 min)

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Legal_annotated_points.pdf (internal summary)

Subject: Re: Redline: order schedule caps/floors + packaging questions

Laura — appreciate the clear positions and the proposed compromise language. A few counterpoints from our side: 

- Netting credits pre-cap is acceptable if we get two assurances: (a) a usage reporting feed that shows raw usage, applied credits, and net billed tokens at invoice-level detail; and (b) the ability to dispute incorrect credit application within 60 days of invoice.
- On per-SKU vs aggregated floors: Velox's preference is non-aggregation given our internal chargeback practices. Aggregation may be acceptable if Redwood can commit to a standard SKU-mapping template and a one-time reconciliation exercise within 45 days after Effective Date.
- Quarterly true-up with a retro settlement cap: 25% feels low given usage variability; propose 40% or alternatively allow 25% but require Redwood to offer a temporary credit line or invoice amortization for rebates owed on true-up settlements greater than $75k.

We can take a 30-minute call Mon 29th 2:00 PM PT. Proposed agenda: 1) Confirm reporting fields and dispute window; 2) Agree on SKU mapping approach and timeline; 3) Finalize settlement cap or amortization option.

Thanks — Morgan
